native.name: Native
native.description: Built-in cache types (f16, q8_0, q4_0, etc.). Maximum compatibility.

turboquant.name: TurboQuant
turboquant.description: Memory saver: Hadamard-rotation KV quantization. 2–4× smaller cache so long chats fit in less RAM; generation is slower than Native.

triattention.name: TriAttention
triattention.description: Sparse attention compressor for long context. Apple Silicon + CUDA.

fbcache.name: First Block Cache
fbcache.description: Diffusion-only cache hook. ~1.8× speedup on DiT pipelines.

taylorseer.name: TaylorSeer
taylorseer.description: Diffusion-only Taylor-expansion cache. Aggressive speedup, FLUX/SD3.

magcache.name: MagCache
magcache.description: Diffusion-only magnitude-based cache. FLUX only without calibration.

fusedAttention.label: Fused attention
fusedAttention.body: Fused attention uses optimized attention kernels when the selected backend supports them. It can improve throughput and reduce overhead, but some model/backend combinations may prefer the standard attention path for compatibility.

dflash.tooltip: DFlash speculative decoding: 3-5x faster generation with zero quality loss.
dflash.label: DFlash
dflash.body: DFlash uses a small draft model to propose multiple tokens in parallel, then verifies them in a single forward pass. This gives 3-5x faster generation with zero quality loss.
dflash.requiresBody: Apple Silicon + dflash-mlx, or Linux/CUDA + dflash. Compatible draft model for the target.
dflash.composerHint: DFlash speculative decoding can ~2× this model with no quality loss.
dflash.ddtreeUnavailable: Not available yet; linear DFlash runs instead.
dflash.treeBudgetTooltip: DDTree: tree-based speculative decoding. 0 = linear DFlash, >0 = explore multiple draft paths in parallel for higher acceptance rates.

fitInMemory.body: Fit in memory asks ChaosEngineAI to choose a runtime/cache profile that keeps the model and KV cache within available memory. Disable it only when you want to force a larger or more aggressive profile and accept possible swapping or load failure.

cacheAdvice.modelExceedsRam: Model weights alone exceed estimated usable RAM. Pick a smaller model or a more aggressive quantisation.
cacheAdvice.nativeF16TooBig: The model can load, but a full native f16 cache at this context may exceed system RAM as the thread fills. Lower context, or pick a compressed strategy.
cacheAdvice.compressedTooBig: The model can load, but the selected context cache may exceed system RAM as the thread fills. Lower context or reduce FP16 layers.
cacheAdvice.vramNativeF16: A full native f16 KV cache at this context is ~{cacheGb} GB, larger than the {vramGb} GB of GPU VRAM available. llama.cpp will spill to system RAM (slow PCIe transfers per token) or fail to allocate. Lower context, drop FP16 layers, or pick the TurboQuant memory saver so the cache fits in VRAM.
cacheAdvice.vramSelected: The selected KV cache at this context is ~{cacheGb} GB, larger than the {vramGb} GB of GPU VRAM available. llama.cpp will spill to system RAM (slow PCIe transfers per token) or fail to allocate. Lower context, drop FP16 layers, or pick the TurboQuant memory saver so the cache fits in VRAM.

tensorfold.tooltip: TensorFold: exact speculative decoding. Drafts from the model's MTP head and/or a draft model are verified against the target model, so replies are identical to serial decoding — only faster.
tensorfold.label: TensorFold (DFlash 2 / MTP drafting)
tensorfold.addVisionTitle: Let this model read attached images (experimental). Adds Pillow, transformers and mlx-vlm to TensorFold's own environment.
tensorfold.memoryShortfall: This checkpoint needs a Mac with at least {needed} GB of memory; this one has {have} GB.
tensorfold.body: TensorFold is a local inference engine with hand-written kernels per model family. It drafts several tokens at a time (from the model's own MTP head and, for some families, a small draft model) and checks every draft against the target model, so the reply is byte-identical to one-token-at-a-time decoding.
tensorfold.requiresBody: Apple Silicon and a separate TensorFold Python environment (installed from this panel). Serves only the checkpoints it is tested with.
tensorfold.memoryBody: {needed} GB of unified memory or more.
tensorfold.statusInstalled: Installed{version} — active when speculative decoding is ticked.
tensorfold.statusNotInstalled: Not installed. Click Install TensorFold to set up its separate environment.
tensorfold.visionInstalled: Installed (experimental) — attach images in chat while TensorFold is ticked. A request with images starts from a fresh KV cache.
tensorfold.visionNotInstalled: Not installed. Reads images with the model's own vision tower. Adds Pillow, transformers and mlx-vlm; TensorFold's authors still mark it experimental.
tensorfold.grammarInstalled: Installed — a JSON schema set in the sampler panel is enforced.
tensorfold.grammarNotInstalled: Not installed. Needed to enforce a JSON schema; without it such requests are refused. Adds PyTorch, which is a large download.
tensorfold.exclusiveBody: No other engine in the app can load this model, so it always runs on TensorFold; the box switches its drafting on and off.

strategyRole.memorySaverTitle: Shrinks the KV cache so long contexts fit in less memory. Generation is slower than Native.

mtplx.tooltip: MTPLX: native MTP speculative decoding. Uses baked-in prediction heads for ~1.8–2.2x faster generation with zero quality loss.
mtplx.label: MTPLX
mtplx.body: MTPLX uses baked-in Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) heads trained directly into the model. At inference time the heads draft 1–3 tokens per forward pass, which are verified in the same pass — no separate draft model needed. Gives ~1.8–2.2x faster generation with zero quality loss.
mtplx.requiresBody: Apple Silicon + MTPLX isolated venv. Model must have baked-in MTP heads (Qwen3.5/3.6, DeepSeek V3/R1, Qwen3-Coder-Next).
mtplx.statusInstalled: Installed — active when speculative decoding is ticked.
mtplx.statusNotInstalled: Not installed. Click Install MTPLX to set up the isolated venv (~500 MB).

ggufMtp.tooltip: GGUF MTP speculative decoding: uses the model's baked-in MTP heads via llama.cpp --spec-type draft-mtp for ~1.8-2.2x faster generation with zero quality loss.
ggufMtp.label: GGUF MTP
ggufMtp.body: This GGUF ships baked-in Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) heads. llama.cpp runs them via --spec-type draft-mtp (PR #22673) — lossless speculative decoding with no separate draft model.

ggufSpec.tooltip: llama.cpp speculative decoding: uses a DFlash / DFlash 2 / EAGLE-3 / MTP drafter shipped beside this GGUF when present, otherwise draft-free n-gram lookup. Lossless — output is verified by the model.
ggufSpec.label: Speculative decoding
ggufSpec.body: If the model folder has a drafter file (mtp-, dflash-, dspark- or eagle3-*.gguf — DFlash 2 drafters use the dflash- prefix), llama.cpp drafts with it. Otherwise it falls back to ngram-mod, which reuses repeated text (code edits, summaries, reasoning echoed into the answer) with no extra model. Every drafted token is verified, so output is unchanged.
ggufSpec.requiresBody: A current llama-server (run scripts/update-llama-cpp.sh). Older binaries fall back to standard decode with a runtime note.

native.description: Full-precision FP16 KV cache. No compression, so it is the fastest and highest-quality choice, and it works with speculative decoding. It uses the most memory at long context. Works with all backends.

triattention.description: Transparent KV cache compression integrated via vLLM. Linux + CUDA only; ChaosEngineAI does not support TriAttention on macOS.
triattention.requires: Linux + CUDA GPU + vLLM backend. Not supported on macOS.
triattention.installHint: Use this only in a Linux/CUDA environment used by ChaosEngineAI, then restart the app.

turboquant.description: Memory saver. Stores the KV cache in 1-4 bits (about 4-5x smaller at 3-bit) so long conversations fit in far less RAM. The trade is speed: expect slower generation than Native, and on MLX it turns off chat-history cache reuse and cannot be combined with speculative decoding. Pick it when a long context will not fit in memory; otherwise stay on Native. On MLX it uses Hadamard rotation + Lloyd-Max codebooks; on GGUF it uses llama-server-turbo.
turboquant.requires: Apple Silicon + MLX for MLX path; llama-server-turbo for GGUF path.
turboquant.installHint: For MLX: install turboquant-mlx-full. For GGUF: run scripts/build-llama-turbo.sh. Then restart ChaosEngineAI.
